title: The crowd's reaction to Prez at 7th and T
summary: Lester came in with something new on every chorus, asked for four-bar breaks, and the audience hollered; Phillips says people still remember that night.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. He said that's where he learned how to play a whole lot of different solos. Because Paul Jones was trying to do that on him with this "I Got Rhythm," you know what I mean. Shit, man, he played "I Got Rhythm," and every time he'd come in, he'd come in with a different feeling. And the drummer we had playing with us, Toy, he was
playing with us at the Hanger Club...
You say he was in the audience that night in D.C.
He was with us at the Hanger Club.
But he wasn't playing with Walter Page and Lester.
No. His drums was out at the club. We just left the job.
So you're talking about this thing, and you said that then Prez came in after Chester, and every one was different.
Yeah. Prez came in with something that they'd never heard before.
Tell us about the reaction of the people.

Oh man, they hollered. Toyer said, 'Man, what is he doin'? Listen, Paul.' Paul said, 'I don't know, man. He's good. He's good.' Prez fell in with the... [SINGS PREZ SOLO]...started swingin' then, you know. Then he started telling the cats to give him some 4-bar breaks. He started makin' some breaks, man! He said 'Give me four.' And he started playing... He played about two or three choruses with breaks, making breaks, you know what I mean.
Yeah, that should have been recorded. Well, in that day that was hell. That was one of the sessions that every time a cat sees me that knows me, says, 'Man, I'll

never forget that night when you brought Prez up there, man." I say, "Yeah." They say, "You told us about him." I say, "Yeah, man. These cats around here called themselves playing saxophone. It didn't excite me, because I've been with one of the best all of my life! See, when he was in short pants, he was playing better than anybody that we ever heard."
